topics.title: Security Desk: Fake Electrum Servers
topics.description: Fake Electrum servers attack old wallets, COLDCARD's postmortem, Ledger's Berlin implants, and a stack of patches to install tonight

slides.heading: Security Desk: Fake Electrum Servers
slides.body: Dozens of new look-alike servers proxy the real ones so they look healthy. If your Electrum is older than 4.8.3, they can show you a fake payment and wait for you to fee-bump it to the attacker.
bullets: Confirmed in the wild by 0xB10C and Andrew Toth: the W45 flaw, now at scale
Super Testnet's take: wallets should use compact block filters, not Electrum servers

slides.heading: COLDCARD's Postmortem
slides.body: A 2021 firmware change left some seeds on a weak random number generator.
bullets: 300 loss tickets from 236 accounts; 15+ reviews and an AI audit missed it
Seeds made with 50+ dice rolls were never affected. Keylabs says the fix is sound

slides.heading: The Rest of a Rough Week
bullets: Ledger: tampered devices confirmed in Berlin, Dubai under investigation. Buy from the maker
Bitcoin Core CVE-2026-117348: a node-stall bug an AI scan found. Fixed in 30.5, 31.3, 32.1; Knots 29.5.1
59% of reachable nodes still lack the Oct 27 fixes (Mike Schmidt)
BTCPay on Docker: emergency nginx update. Bisq 2.1.16: Java4Shell fix, needed to trade
#FREESAMOURAI's LND node on a Contabo VPS was drained, days after Contabo's own breach
Chainflip's BTC vault lost 122.86 BTC. A vibe-coded wallet sent 1 BTC to anyone-can-spend; mononaut saved it

topics.title: Witness Encryption: A Lock That Opens for a Proof
topics.description: A Stanford/Babylon preprint claims practical witness encryption; Super Testnet says "there goes the game"; experts say wait for peer review

slides.heading: Witness Encryption: A Lock That Opens for a Proof
slides.body: Lock a secret to a statement instead of a key: whoever can prove the statement can open it. Put a bitcoin key inside, and coins unlock for anyone with a valid proof. No operators.
bullets: Praxis (David Tse, Stanford/Babylon, Nov 23): 7.88 GiB ciphertext, Lean 4 proofs
Not peer reviewed yet, and it needs an honest trusted setup

slides.heading: "Well, There Goes the Game"
slides.body: Super Testnet: "If witness encryption is solved then bitcoin is ethereum." He expects recycled DeFi with a "now on bitcoin!" sticker, and people losing money.
bullets: Robin Linus: it would "fundamentally improve Bitcoin bridges" if it survives review
waxwing: "truly groundbreaking" if nothing's wrong, with real limits

slides.heading: Discussion
slides.body: If a proof can unlock coins without a soft fork, do we still need covenants? Is "anything Ethereum can do, on Bitcoin" a win, or a new way to lose money?

topics.title: Bitcoin Dev: Core and Lightning
topics.description: Core 31.3 and 30.5, a wallet fingerprint removed, Core Lightning's biggest release, LND fixes, and a Taproot Assets deadline

slides.heading: Bitcoin Dev: Core and Lightning
bullets: Core 31.3 / 30.5 out; Optech #432: a Tor/I2P address leak fixed
Core master: fee bumps stop backdating locktime (a wallet fingerprint); encryptwallet deprecated for old wallets
Core Lightning v26.12rc1: 832 commits after a year of bug reports; pay gives way to xpay
LND: fixes for a reconnect force-close and missed close confirmations
Taproot Assets: upgrade and close asset channels before block 978,493 (about Dec 2)
Bark 0.9.0: Ark wallets now speak Nostr Wallet Connect

slides.heading: Quantum Homework and Core Maintenance
bullets: Blockstream: switch commitments, a possible soft fork to guard Liquid's hidden amounts from quantum attacks
SHRINCS, the hash-based post-quantum signature idea, gets its first security analysis draft
Core #36908: the Stratum V2 mining interface no longer crashes a fresh node
fanquake's four years at Brink: ~2,600 merges, 20+ Core releases. Thank you

Public Pool's first block in 138 days (977,488) paid one small miner 3.178 BTC
Canaan open-sourced the Avalon Nano 3s firmware (MIT, alpha)
One-click DATUM in Foreman: build your own block templates. Foundry reportedly testing Stratum V2
Kalshi now lists CFTC-certified bets on the difficulty adjustment

topics.title: Policy Corner: Self-Custody, Squeezed and Defended
topics.description: The Philippines and South Korea restrict transfers to your own wallet; France and Ukraine push the other way; FinCEN gets breached

slides.heading: Policy Corner: Self-Custody, Squeezed and Defended
bullets: Coins.ph stopped transfers to self-custody wallets Nov 19 (Philippine Travel Rule)
South Korea: from Feb 19, 2027, personal-wallet transfers generally only to yourself
France's Senate rejected a register of €100K+ self-custody wallets: a target list for kidnappers
Ukraine passed its crypto law (271 votes): legal and taxed from July 2027, holdings not declared

slides.heading: Also on the Desk
bullets: FinCEN, home of every suspicious-activity report, disclosed a "cybersecurity incident"
CFTC staff: bitcoin can count toward an exchange's operating-cost reserves
Hong Kong custody licensing bill; UK bans exchange self-market-making from Oct 2027
Michigan bills would ban crypto kiosks outright
slides.body: If your exchange stopped withdrawals to your own wallet tomorrow, where would your coins be?

topics.title: AI Corner: Can't Look vs. Promise Not To
topics.description: Canary prompts catch AI providers leaking, agents pay in sats with guardrails, and open models small enough to run at home

slides.heading: AI Corner: Can't Look vs. Promise Not To
slides.body: 2 million planted canary prompts: stolen keys were tried within hours, even "Zero Data Retention" prompts were read. A promise not to look isn't privacy.
bullets: OpenRouter dropped three providers. Maple ($5.3M seed) runs models in enclaves you can verify
Run it at home: Inkling 2 Mini (32 GB Mac), Ternary Bonsai 27B (5.93 GB)
Haller-1 reads handwritten seed words offline on a SeedSigner (proof of concept)

slides.heading: Agents Pay in Sats, Safely
bullets: l402-bridge: coding agents buy inference in sats from an NWC wallet, with caps
nwc-guard: a firewall that asks your phone before an agent pays
l402-receipts: "Don't trust the meter, verify it": receipts anchored on Nostr and Bitcoin
ngx-l402 v1.4.0 charges per MCP tool call; an AI agent bought satsboard's billboard for 29 sats

topics.title: Builder Spotlight: OpenBazaar Is Back
topics.description: The freedom-tech marketplace returns in Rust over Tor, and how it stacks up against Shopstr, Plebeian Market and LNbits Nostr Market

slides.heading: Builder Spotlight: OpenBazaar Is Back
slides.body: Rewritten in Rust, over Tor, with no company in the middle of your sale.
bullets: Escrow where the moderator holds no key, only picks a pre-signed payout
Testnet4 alpha (MIT): test coins only, no real money yet

slides.heading: How It Works
bullets: Your shop belongs to recovery words only you hold; buyers pay the seller's wallet
Signed listings: a fake node can hide them, not forge them
Sybil defense is a BTC fee checked on chain: "we won't do KYC"
Honest about gaps: self-reviews still possible, no seller bond yet

slides.heading: Bitcoin Marketplaces, Side by Side
slides.body: I've used Shopstr and know the team. How they compare:
bullets: OpenBazaar: its own app over Tor; escrow on chain; a BTC fee keeps out fakes. Testnet4 alpha
Shopstr: listings on Nostr (NIP-99); pay by Lightning or Cashu; reviews and DMs on Nostr. Live since 2023
Plebeian Market: a Nostr marketplace, being rebuilt; auctions in research
LNbits Nostr Market: run your stall from your own LNbits (NIP-15). v1.2.1 on Nov 10
Buying bitcoin, not goods: RoboSats (Lightning over Tor) and Mostro (on Nostr)

slides.heading: Discussion
slides.body: Open listings on Nostr, or OpenBazaar's own network: which one wins buyers? Who here has bought or sold on Shopstr? What would you sell for sats?

topics.title: Max's Corner: Guard Dog & Trust Issues
topics.description: Week two of my two open-source security tools: what landed, what's in review, and where I'd love your help

slides.heading: Max's Corner: Guard Dog & Trust Issues
slides.body: Week two. This week's news is exactly why I'm building these.
bullets: Fake Electrum servers: Trust Issues never trusts one server
COLDCARD: 15+ reviews missed it. Guard Dog is graded by tests written first

slides.heading: Guard Dog: What Landed, What's Next
bullets: 12 pull requests merged: reads advisories, checks version ranges, read-only node logins
13 services it knows, incl. BTCPay, Alby Hub, Fedimint, Taproot Assets, umbrelOS
In review: version readers, the catalog loader, alerts as private Nostr DMs (NIP-17)
Two AI reviewers read every change; it merges only at zero high or medium findings
Next: the matcher, so the first real finding lands end to end. Today: 0 of 9, honestly

slides.heading: Trust Issues, and Where I'd Love Help
slides.body: "An explorer can lie, it just can't fool your node."
bullets: Trust Issues now logs every RPC call and shows unsupported ones on /status
Still signet only: mainnet stays refused in code until someone outside reviews it
Umbrel or StartOS user? How do you list installed apps without admin?
How long should a new release wait before Guard Dog calls it safest? I'm starting at 7 days
